title: Prescribing Under a Massachusetts Collaborative Practice Agreement
topic: Collaborative practice / Prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement
subtopic: The three-fold power in the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) and the ten numbered requirements the proviso attaches to it, including the purpose-specific Department registration in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2), the particulars supplied to a dispensing pharmacist under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), the facility medication order in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) and the 24-hour copy to the supervising physician under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10); and the additional conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) where prescriptive practices are included in the agreement
learning_objectives: State the three acts the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorise and explain why authority to do one of them is not authority to do another.

Explain what the proviso closing the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) does to the numbered paragraphs that follow it, and separate the paragraphs that state duties from those that state permissions carrying their own conditions.
Name all ten numbered requirements in 105 CMR 700.003(G) and decide which of them bear on a given set of facts.
Apply the purpose element in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) to a pharmacist who already holds a Department controlled substance registration obtained for some other activity.
Say what the DEA limb of 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires, what qualifies it, and what the regulation leaves to the federal scheme.
List the three conditions 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) adds where prescriptive practices are included in the agreement, and say what each one is fastened to.
Distinguish the Department registration required by 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) from the controlled substance registration required by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1.

Recite the particulars a prescribing pharmacist supplies to a dispensing pharmacist under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), identify the one no ordinary practitioner prescription carries, and say on whom the paragraph puts its duty.
State the duty in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10): what has to be copied, to whom, from what event the 24 hours are measured, and what displaces the period.
Choose the correct instrument for a patient in a licensed health facility and state where the writing must be entered.
Name the boundary between this section and the separate retail collaborative practice regime.

orientation.text: Massachusetts locates a pharmacist's prescribing authority in 105 CMR 700.003, the Department of Public Health section on registration of persons for a specific activity, and the paragraph that carries the authority is 105 CMR 700.003(G). Its opening words are the whole of the power: a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, provided the following requirements are met. Two things follow from that single sentence and both are examinable. The power is three-fold, and the words as authorized in attach to each of the three acts separately rather than to the bundle. And the sentence closes on a proviso, so the numbered paragraphs that follow are not commentary on the power; they are the requirements it is granted subject to. Read them with care, because they are not all cast the same way. Some speak to the pharmacist as plain duties, and others state something the pharmacist may do and hedge it with a condition of its own, so a permission the pharmacist never relies on is not a requirement she has broken. But a requirement that does bear on the facts and is not met leaves her without the power rather than exercising it imperfectly.

Read the three acts as three separate permissions. Issuing starts a prescription or medication order. Modifying changes one that already exists. Discontinuing stops the therapy. Nothing in the opening words ranks them by gravity, and nothing makes the smaller act a component of the larger one, so the intuition that a pharmacist trusted to change a dose must also be trusted to stop the drug has no foothold in the text. Discontinuation in particular is a regulated prescribing act and not a clinical judgement sitting outside the regulation, which is why an agreement silent on discontinuation leaves the pharmacist without authority to discontinue no matter how plainly the clinical case for stopping is made out. The other half of the opening words does comparable work on the agreement itself: the agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, three named instruments read conjunctively, so an agreement answering one of them but not the others is not an agreement this paragraph recognises.

It is worth having the whole of 105 CMR 700.003(G) in view, because a paragraph that presents itself as a list of requirements invites the reader to assume the list has been covered. There are ten numbered requirements. (1) the pharmacist meets all applicable requirements of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00. (2) the pharmacist registers with the Department, and with the DEA if applicable, for the purpose of prescribing. (3) the pharmacist issues, modifies or discontinues in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and the agreement itself. (4) a pharmacist practising in a retail setting may issue a prescription for a controlled substance in Schedule VI only. (5) and (6) govern dispensing a controlled substance for immediate treatment and the stock the pharmacist may obtain for that purpose. (7) governs the particulars supplied to a dispensing pharmacist. (8) governs the medication order for a patient in a licensed health facility. (9) requires a record of any controlled substance maintained for dispensing for immediate treatment or administering. (10) requires a copy of an initial prescription, or of a modification or discontinuation, to reach the supervising physician within 24 hours of its issuance. Notice how differently they are cast: (1), (2), (3), (9) and (10) speak to the pharmacist as duties, while (4) through (8) state what the pharmacist may do and attach conditions to the doing.

Two of those requirements do quiet work that is easy to miss. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(1) makes the Department's prescribing power depend on the pharmacist meeting all applicable requirements of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00, and the range matters: it is the whole of 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00 and not the collaborative practice regulation alone, so a Board of Pharmacy failure elsewhere in that body of regulation is a failure of a condition on prescribing. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3) then turns from the pharmacist to the act. The pharmacist issues, modifies or discontinues a prescription or medication order in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and the collaborative practice agreement between the pharmacist and supervising physician. So the opening words ask whether the agreement authorises the act, subparagraph (1) asks whether the pharmacist is in good order with her own board, and subparagraph (3) asks whether the act as performed conformed to each of those instruments and to the agreement. A prescription written outside the agreement's terms fails (3) even where every registration is in order.

Several of the numbered requirements concern controlled substances the pharmacist holds, or the schedules she may reach, rather than the mechanics of a particular prescription. Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(5) the pharmacist may dispense a controlled substance for immediate treatment in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9, provided the pharmacist is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(G) to prescribe that substance, so the dispensing permission is parasitic on the prescribing authority and does not enlarge it. Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6) the pharmacist may order from a drug wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor, for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment, those controlled substances in Schedule VI which she is authorized to prescribe; and for dispensing Schedules II through V for immediate treatment the same subparagraph allows her to obtain those substances only as supplied by the supervising physician or obtained through a prescription or medication order for the patient, which is a supply route rather than a purchase. Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) she maintains a record of any controlled substance maintained for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment or administering pursuant to 105 CMR 700.000 and any related Department guidelines. And 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) adds the Department's own ceiling for one setting: a pharmacist practising in a retail setting may issue a prescription for a controlled substance in Schedule VI only.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) earns a paragraph of its own, because the words it turns on are easy to read past. It requires that the pharmacist registers with the Department, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000. The load-bearing words are for the purpose of prescribing. A pharmacist may already hold a Department controlled substance registration obtained for some other activity, and the paragraph declines to treat a registration as one undifferentiated permission to handle controlled substances: the purpose for which the registration was taken out is part of the requirement, so a registration obtained so that a pharmacy could dispense does not carry prescribing authority across to a collaborating pharmacist. The federal limb is drafted differently again. It is expressly conditional, the pharmacist registering with the DEA if applicable, so it does not attach to every collaborating pharmacist merely because an agreement exists; and the regulation refers the question of when it does apply out to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 rather than answering it in its own terms, which means the answer turns on what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

A second registration requirement comes from the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and is easily conflated with the first. 247 CMR 16.02(1) sets out the qualifications a pharmacist must satisfy to enter into a collaborative practice agreement and engage in collaborative practice, and 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) adds three further conditions, but only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement. The first is to maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000. The second is to complete training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) prior to initially obtaining a controlled substance registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence. The third is to submit an attestation, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth, in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Notice what each condition is fastened to, because that is where the examinable difference sits: the registration to the term of the agreement, the training to the renewal of the pharmacist licence, and the attestation to a state of affairs the pharmacist swears to. The other qualifications listed in 247 CMR 16.02(1) apply to every collaborating pharmacist and belong to the companion section on who may practise; only subparagraph (f) is triggered by prescriptive practices.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) governs what happens when the prescription leaves the prescribing pharmacist and reaches someone who will fill it. The pharmacist may issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20, which is the general law's oral prescription provision, provided that the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies their name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides their registration number, work address, phone number, and the name of the supervising physician. Two things are clearly identified and four things are provided, and every one of the six runs to the dispensing pharmacist rather than to the patient, which is what a transmission between two pharmacists looks like. Three of the four provided particulars are the sort of thing any prescriber supplies. The work address is stated as a work address, so a home address or a mobile number offered in its place does not answer the paragraph. The distinctive particular is the last one, the name of the supervising physician, which an ordinary practitioner prescription never carries and which the pharmacist's own prescribing authority does not dispense with. The duty is the prescribing pharmacist's: the paragraph makes these particulars the proviso on which she may issue at all, and says nothing about what the dispensing pharmacist must do. The consequence for the receiving pharmacist follows from that rather than from any duty of her own. A transmission that omits one of the six is not a transmission the paragraph authorised, so there is no question of weighing how material the omission seemed; there is nothing properly issued to fill until the missing particular has been supplied.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) is the only requirement in the paragraph fastened to a clock, and it is the one a candidate revising the deadlines of collaborative prescribing is looking for. The pharmacist provides a copy of an initial prescription or a modification or discontinuation of a prescription to the supervising physician within 24 hours of its issuance, unless more urgent notification is required under the circumstances. Four things decide questions on it. The duty is the pharmacist's: the paragraph does not put it on the dispensing pharmacy or on the physician to ask. The 24 hours run from issuance, so the clock starts when the prescription is issued rather than when it is filled or when the pharmacist next happens to speak to the physician. The subject matter is not confined to a new prescription, because a modification and a discontinuation each carry the same copy duty, which is what one would expect of a paragraph that opens by authorising all three acts. And the proviso runs in one direction only: where the circumstances require more urgent notification, 24 hours is not the standard, and nothing in the words lets the period run longer.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) deals with the opposite situation, a patient who will not be carrying a prescription to a pharmacy because the patient is inside a licensed health facility. There the pharmacist may prescribe a controlled substance for the patient through the use of a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided that such a written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000. Three elements decide questions on this paragraph. The instrument is a written medication order, not an outpatient prescription form and not an oral instruction. The place is the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, not a record the pharmacy or the pharmacist keeps and not a note left with staff. And the gate is that the facility is a licensed health facility; the paragraph names a hospital, a long term care facility, an ambulatory care clinic and a hospice, introducing them with the word including, so those four are an illustration of the class rather than the class itself, and a setting that holds no health facility licence falls outside the paragraph however carefully it maintains care records of its own.

This section is the prescribing act together with the requirements 105 CMR 700.003(G) attaches to it. It does not decide what collaborative drug therapy management is or who may enter into an agreement, and it does not decide what the agreement document must contain; those are the subjects of the companion sections on the practice and on the agreement, and a question about qualifications, referral, consent or required agreement terms is answered there. The one qualification provision set out here is 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f), because it is triggered by the inclusion of prescriptive practices. This section also stops short of the retail regime. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) states the Department's own ceiling for a pharmacist practising in a retail setting and is set out here with the other numbered requirements, but the rest of that regime, meaning who may be a patient there, which disease states may be co-managed, the extension of current therapy, the vaccine limb, and the referral and consent formalities, is the retail section's material and is not supplied below. Where a question turns on any of those, take the answer from that section rather than inferring it from anything here.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement authorises a pharmacist to issue prescriptions for a referred patient's hypertension and to discontinue therapy where a listed adverse effect appears. It says nothing about changing doses. Reviewing the patient, the pharmacist concludes that the current dose should be halved rather than stopped. May she halve it?
steps: Return to the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G): a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement.
Separate the three acts. This agreement addresses issuing and discontinuing, and modifying is a distinct act rather than a lesser instance of either of them.
Resist the direction of travel in the facts. Halving a dose looks more conservative than stopping the drug, but conservatism is not the test the paragraph applies; authorisation act by act is.
Check the remaining route. Discontinuation is authorised, so stopping the drug is within the agreement, but that does not convert into a power to leave the patient on a changed dose.
worked_examples.resolution: She may not modify the dose under this agreement. The error the scenario invites is ranking the three acts by clinical gravity and assuming authority to do the graver act carries authority to do the milder one; the opening words authorise each act only as authorized in the agreement, so the agreement has to be amended before she can modify.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist holds a current Department controlled substance registration that her employer obtained years ago so that the pharmacy could dispense. She now signs a collaborative practice agreement that includes prescriptive practices and proposes to prescribe. She reasons that a controlled substance registration is a controlled substance registration. What is missing?
steps: Read 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) as a whole: the pharmacist registers with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
Test her registration against the purpose element rather than against its currency. It is current, but it was obtained for dispensing, and the purpose is part of the requirement.

Now add the Board's overlay, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

Keep the two registration requirements apart. One is a condition on the prescribing power in the Department's regulation; the other is a qualification in the Board's regulation that runs for the term of the agreement.
worked_examples.resolution: She needs Department registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices, the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) as well. The error the scenario invites is treating a controlled substance registration as one undifferentiated permission, so that an instrument held for another purpose is read as covering this one.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist telephones a prescription to a pharmacy across town. She gives her name, says she is a pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement, gives her registration number, names her supervising physician, and offers her mobile number, saying she moves between sites and has no fixed work address to give. The receiving pharmacist is minded to fill it.
steps: List what 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) requires: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, and registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician provided.
Mark off what was supplied. Name, designation, registration number, supervising physician and a phone number are all present.
Identify what is absent. The paragraph specifies a work address as a particular in its own right, alongside the phone number, so a contact number does not stand in for it.

Treat the proviso as a condition on the pharmacist's power to issue rather than as a checklist of good practice, which means the transmission as it stands is not one 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) authorised her to make.
worked_examples.resolution: The work address has to be supplied before the prescription is one the paragraph authorised her to issue, so the receiving pharmacist cannot fill it as transmitted. The error the scenario invites is substituting one particular for another on the reasoning that the prescriber is reachable anyway, when the paragraph lists the work address and the phone number as separate items and conditions the pharmacist's power to issue on all of them being supplied.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist prescribes a controlled substance for a patient of a licensed hospice under an agreement that authorises her to do so. She writes a medication order rather than a prescription, but files it in the collaborative practice file her pharmacy department keeps for the hospice, and tells the hospice nurse the order is on file. Has she used the paragraph correctly?
steps: Confirm the setting first. A hospice is among the licensed health facilities 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) names, so the paragraph is available to her.
Confirm the instrument. She wrote a medication order rather than an outpatient prescription form, which is what the paragraph calls for.
Test the location of the writing, which is the element she has got wrong: the paragraph requires the written medication order to be entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.
Note the closing condition as well, that such a written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000, so getting the instrument right does not exhaust the paragraph.
worked_examples.resolution: She has used the right instrument in the right kind of setting but has entered it in the wrong record, so the paragraph is not satisfied until the order is entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the hospice. The error the scenario invites is treating the medication order as a document the pharmacy owns and files, when the paragraph fixes both the instrument and the record it must live on.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist practises under an agreement at a licensed ambulatory care clinic, where she prescribes for referred patients by medication order. One patient is leaving the clinic and needs the same therapy dispensed by a community pharmacy near home. The pharmacist proposes to write the same medication order and let the patient take a copy to that pharmacy. What has to change, and what cannot be decided from this section?
steps: Separate the two instruments. Inside the clinic, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.

Recognise that a prescription reaching a pharmacy for dispensing is the subject of a different paragraph, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), which permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20.

Attach the particulars to the second route: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, plus registration number, work address, phone number and the supervising physician's name.

Notice where the schedule ceiling attaches. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) fixes its Schedule VI ceiling to a pharmacist practising in a retail setting, and this pharmacist practises in the clinic rather than in the pharmacy that will dispense, so the ceiling is fastened to where the prescriber practises and not to where the prescription is filled. What else the retail regime requires is the companion section's subject.
worked_examples.resolution: The instrument must change: a facility medication order does not travel, and issuing to a dispensing pharmacy engages 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) and its particulars. The error the scenario invites is carrying an instrument that worked in one setting into another, and the further trap is reading the Schedule VI ceiling in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) off the pharmacy that will dispense rather than off the setting in which the prescriber practises.

worked_examples.scenario: Under an agreement that authorises her to modify and to discontinue therapy, a collaborating pharmacist reviews a co-managed patient on a Friday morning and discontinues one of his two antihypertensives, issuing the discontinuation at nine o'clock. She notes the change in her own record and plans to raise it with the supervising physician at the multidisciplinary meeting the following Wednesday, telling the patient his physician will hear about it then. Nothing in the patient's presentation is urgent.
steps: Confirm the act is authorised. The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) permit issuing, modifying and discontinuing only as authorized in the agreement, and this agreement authorises discontinuation.

Now run the numbered requirements that bear on the facts. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) requires the pharmacist to provide a copy of an initial prescription or a modification or discontinuation of a prescription to the supervising physician within 24 hours of its issuance.

Check the subject matter and the recipient before the timing. A discontinuation is expressly within the duty, and the copy goes to the supervising physician rather than into the pharmacist's own record.
Measure the period from the right event. The 24 hours run from issuance, which was Friday at nine o'clock, not from the next scheduled meeting, so Wednesday is several days outside the period.

Read the proviso in the right direction. More urgent notification is required where the circumstances call for it; nothing in these facts makes the case more urgent, and the proviso could not have made the period longer in any event.
worked_examples.resolution: The discontinuation itself is within her authority, but waiting for the Wednesday meeting breaks 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10), which requires the copy to reach the supervising physician within 24 hours of issuance. The error the scenario invites is treating the copy as a courtesy that can wait for the next scheduled contact, and measuring the period from that contact rather than from issuance.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist in a licensed hospital keeps a small stock of a Schedule VI product and of a Schedule IV product so that she can dispense for immediate treatment under her agreement. She orders both from the hospital's usual wholesaler, keeps the Schedule VI stock on a running record and treats the Schedule IV stock as covered by the ward's ordinary controlled drug book. She is authorised by the agreement to prescribe both products.
steps: Start with the permission. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(5) lets her dispense a controlled substance for immediate treatment in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9 provided she is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(G) to prescribe that substance, which she is.

Now read the supply route in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6). She may order from a wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor only those controlled substances in Schedule VI which she is authorized to prescribe, so the Schedule VI order is within the subparagraph.

Apply the second half of the same subparagraph to the Schedule IV product. For dispensing Schedules II through V for immediate treatment she may obtain the substance only as supplied by the supervising physician or obtained through a prescription or medication order for the patient, so ordering it from the wholesaler is outside the route the subparagraph allows.

Finish with the record. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires a record of any controlled substance maintained for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment or administering, which reaches both products and is not answered by pointing at a record kept for another purpose.
worked_examples.resolution: The Schedule VI stock is properly obtained and the Schedule IV stock is not, because 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6) confines Schedule II through V material held for immediate treatment to what the supervising physician supplies or what comes through a prescription or medication order for the patient; and 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires her own record of everything she maintains for that purpose. The error the scenario invites is reading authority to prescribe a substance as authority to buy it in for immediate treatment, and treating a record kept by the ward as the record the subparagraph asks her to maintain.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) let a pharmacist do which three things to a prescription or medication order?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Issue, modify or discontinue it, in each case as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an agreement that authorises a pharmacist to modify a therapy also authorises the pharmacist to discontinue it.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The three acts are stated in parallel and each is exercisable only as authorized in the agreement, so authority to modify does not carry authority to discontinue.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What do the words that close the opening sentence of 105 CMR 700.003(G) do to the numbered paragraphs beneath it?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The sentence ends provided the following requirements are met, so the numbered paragraphs are conditions on the power rather than commentary about it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How many numbered requirements does 105 CMR 700.003(G) carry, and which of them are cast as duties on the pharmacist?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Ten. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(1), (2), (3), (9) and (10) are cast as duties on the pharmacist; (4) through (8) state what the pharmacist may do and attach conditions to the doing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(1) require, and over what range of regulation?
retrieval_prompts.answer: That the pharmacist meets all applicable requirements of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00, so the range is the whole of 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00 rather than the collaborative practice regulation alone.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3) requires the act itself to be in accordance with what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and the collaborative practice agreement between the pharmacist and the supervising physician.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) the pharmacist registers with the Department in accordance with ______, and with the DEA ______, for the purpose of ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 105 CMR 700.004; if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300; prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacist already holds a current Department controlled substance registration obtained so her pharmacy could dispense. What does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) still require of her before she prescribes?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Registration with the Department for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000. The purpose the registration was obtained for is part of the requirement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which three conditions does 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) add, and what triggers them?
retrieval_prompts.answer: They are triggered if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement: maintain a current Department controlled substance registration during the term of the agreement; complete the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence; and submit an attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury about participation in MassHealth.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The biennial training required by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2. is a condition precedent to renewing what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The pharmacist licence, not merely the collaborative practice agreement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: List the particulars 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) requires the prescribing pharmacist to give the dispensing pharmacist.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Name and professional designation clearly identified, and registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician provided.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which particular in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) has no counterpart on an ordinary practitioner prescription?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The name of the supervising physician.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: For a patient in a licensed health facility, what instrument does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorise and where must it be entered?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written medication order, entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and it must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which facilities does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) name, and is the list exhaustive?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A hospital, long term care facility, ambulatory care clinic or hospice. They are introduced by including, so they illustrate the class; the operative gate is that the facility is a licensed health facility.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10), what must be copied, to whom, and within what period measured from what event?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A copy of an initial prescription, or of a modification or discontinuation of a prescription, to the supervising physician, within 24 hours of its issuance, unless more urgent notification is required under the circumstances.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: the proviso in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) can give a pharmacist longer than 24 hours.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The proviso is that more urgent notification may be required under the circumstances, so it can only shorten the period; the outer limit stays 24 hours from issuance.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: For dispensing for immediate treatment, where may a collaborating pharmacist obtain a Schedule IV substance, and where may she obtain a Schedule VI one?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6), Schedules II through V may be obtained only as supplied by the supervising physician or through a prescription or medication order for the patient; Schedule VI substances she is authorized to prescribe may be ordered from a drug wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires a record of any controlled substance so maintained.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What ceiling does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) place on a pharmacist practising in a retail setting?
retrieval_prompts.answer: She may issue a prescription for a controlled substance in Schedule VI only, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3).

quick_review.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G) opens by permitting a pharmacist to issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement, and closes on the words provided the following requirements are met.
Each of the three acts must be found in the agreement separately; the acts are stated in parallel, so none of them implies another.
The agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 together, not one of them at the drafter's choice.
105 CMR 700.003(G) carries ten numbered requirements; (1), (2), (3), (9) and (10) are stated as duties on the pharmacist and (4) through (8) as permissions carrying conditions of their own.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(1) requires the pharmacist to meet all applicable Board of Registration in Pharmacy requirements established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00.
105 CMR 700.003(G)(3) requires the prescribing act itself to be in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and the agreement.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and with the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
A Department registration obtained for a different activity does not carry prescribing authority, because the purpose forms part of the requirement.
The DEA limb is qualified by the words if applicable, so it binds according to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 and not by virtue of the collaborative practice agreement.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) attaches three conditions, and only where prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement.

Those conditions are a Department controlled substance registration maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and a sworn MassHealth attestation.
The section 18(e) training is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, which ties a prescriptive-practice condition to the licence rather than to the agreement.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 provided the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.
The particulars in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) run to the dispensing pharmacist, and the work address is listed separately from the phone number.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility through a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided the order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.
105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) permits a pharmacist practising in a retail setting to issue a prescription for a controlled substance in Schedule VI only.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(5) and (6) allow dispensing for immediate treatment only of what the pharmacist is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(G) to prescribe, and allow Schedules II through V held for that purpose to be obtained only as supplied by the supervising physician or through a prescription or medication order for the patient.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires a record of any controlled substance maintained for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment or administering pursuant to 105 CMR 700.000 and any related Department guidelines.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) requires the pharmacist to provide a copy of an initial prescription, or of a modification or discontinuation, to the supervising physician within 24 hours of its issuance, unless more urgent notification is required under the circumstances.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist proposes to act on a patient's drug therapy under a collaborative practice agreement.
decision_logic.action: Name the act first: issuing, modifying or discontinuing. Then look for that act, by name, in the agreement, because 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorises each one only as authorized in the agreement.

decision_logic.condition: The agreement authorises the act, and the question is whether the pharmacist may exercise the power at all.
decision_logic.action: Treat the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as the requirements the power is granted subject to, since the opening words end provided the following requirements are met, and work through the ones that bear on the facts. There are ten of them: (1), (2), (3), (9) and (10) are duties, and (4) through (8) are permissions with conditions of their own, so a permission she never relies on is not a requirement she has failed.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacist already holds a Department controlled substance registration.
decision_logic.action: Ask what purpose it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, so a registration held for another activity does not satisfy it.

decision_logic.condition: A question asks whether the collaborating pharmacist needs DEA registration.
decision_logic.action: Do not answer yes or no on the strength of the agreement. The limb applies if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, so ask what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

Add the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f): the controlled substance registration maintained during the term, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

decision_logic.condition: The prescription is being transmitted to a pharmacist who will dispense it.
decision_logic.action: Check the transmission against the list in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) item by item, and where a particular is missing, obtain it rather than assess how material it was.

decision_logic.condition: The patient is in a facility.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the facility is a licensed health facility. If it is, use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8); if it is not, that paragraph does not supply the instrument.

decision_logic.condition: The question turns on which schedules a pharmacist in a community or retail pharmacy may prescribe.
decision_logic.action: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) gives the Department's own answer for the retail setting: a prescription for a controlled substance in Schedule VI only. Everything else about that regime, meaning the patient conditions, the disease states, the extension of current therapy and the referral and consent formalities, is the retail section's material rather than this one's.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacist has issued, modified or discontinued a prescription.
decision_logic.action: Start the clock at issuance and get a copy to the supervising physician inside 24 hours under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10), and sooner where the circumstances require more urgent notification. Do not measure from the next ward round, the next clinic or the next time the physician is reached.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacist wants to hold a controlled substance so that she can dispense for immediate treatment.
decision_logic.action: Ask two questions in order. Is she authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(G) to prescribe that substance, which 105 CMR 700.003(G)(5) makes the condition of dispensing it for immediate treatment? And where is the stock to come from: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6) allows Schedule VI to be ordered from a wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor, and allows Schedules II through V only as supplied by the supervising physician or through a prescription or medication order for the patient. Then keep the record 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires.

ma_vs_federal.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) makes a federal registration part of a Massachusetts condition: the pharmacist registers with the Department and with the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300. Massachusetts therefore treats the federal registration as one of the conditions on its own prescribing power rather than leaving it to federal enforcement alone.

The federal limb is incorporated conditionally. The regulation does not itself state when DEA registration is applicable; it refers that question to 21 CFR 1300, so the Massachusetts requirement is as wide, and no wider, as the federal scheme makes it.

exceptions.text: The DEA limb of 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) applies only if applicable, so it is not a universal precondition of prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement.

The three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) bite only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement; an agreement without prescriptive practices does not attract them.

The medication order route in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) is available only where the patient is in a licensed health facility, so the instrument it authorises is unavailable in a setting that holds no such licence.
The 24-hour period in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) yields where more urgent notification is required under the circumstances, so the proviso shortens the period rather than extending it.
105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) is addressed to a pharmacist practising in a retail setting and states no schedule ceiling for a pharmacist practising elsewhere.

The wholesaler route in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6) is open only for Schedule VI substances the pharmacist is authorized to prescribe; Schedules II through V held for dispensing for immediate treatment come only from the supervising physician or through a prescription or medication order for the patient.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacist exercises the prescribing power under a collaborative practice agreement
timing_deadlines.timeframe: The Department registration must be held, for the purpose of prescribing, at the time the power is exercised
timing_deadlines.consequence: Without a registration taken out for that purpose the condition in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is unmet and the power in 105 CMR 700.003(G) is not available.

timing_deadlines.event: Agreement including prescriptive practices is in force
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Throughout the term of the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained for the whole term, so allowing it to lapse mid-term breaks the qualification.

timing_deadlines.event: Training required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Before initially obtaining the controlled substance registration, and at least biennially thereafter
timing_deadlines.consequence: Completion is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2., so the consequence of missing it falls on the licence and not only on the agreement.

timing_deadlines.event: Copy of an initial prescription, or of a modification or discontinuation, to the supervising physician
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 24 hours of its issuance, unless more urgent notification is required under the circumstances
timing_deadlines.consequence: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) is one of the numbered requirements the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) attach to the prescribing power, so a copy that reaches the supervising physician late leaves a requirement of the paragraph unmet. The period runs from issuance, and the proviso can only shorten it.

forms_records.text: The collaborative practice agreement is the instrument that authorises the prescribing act, and it must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Each of issuing, modifying and discontinuing must appear in it before the pharmacist may do that thing.

A Department registration obtained in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000 is the instrument 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires; the purpose recorded for it is part of what makes it sufficient.
A DEA registration in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 is required by the same paragraph where the federal limb is applicable.

Where prescriptive practices are included, a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department, held pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000, must be maintained during the term of the agreement.

Where prescriptive practices are included, the pharmacist submits an attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

A prescription issued under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) is issued in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 and carries with it, to the dispensing pharmacist, the prescribing pharmacist's name and professional designation, registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

For a patient in a licensed health facility the instrument is a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and that written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.
A copy of the initial prescription, or of the modification or discontinuation, is the document 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) requires to reach the supervising physician within 24 hours of issuance.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) requires a record of any controlled substance maintained for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment or administering pursuant to 105 CMR 700.000 and any related Department guidelines.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement
role_duties.duty: Exercise only those of the three acts, issuing, modifying and discontinuing, that the agreement authorises, and treat the numbered requirements in 105 CMR 700.003(G) as conditions on the power rather than as guidance.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist seeking to prescribe under 105 CMR 700.003(G)
role_duties.duty: Register with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and with the DEA in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 where that limb is applicable.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist whose agreement includes prescriptive practices
role_duties.duty: Maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department for the whole term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist obtaining or renewing a controlled substance registration for prescriptive practice
role_duties.duty: Complete the training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) before initially obtaining the registration and at least biennially thereafter, this being a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence.

Submit the MassHealth participation attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, the attestation covering either participation as a provider of services or the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

role_duties.role: Prescribing pharmacist transmitting a prescription for another pharmacy to fill
role_duties.duty: Clearly identify name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provide registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

role_duties.role: Dispensing pharmacist receiving a prescription from a collaborating pharmacist
role_duties.duty: Read 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) as placing its duty on the prescribing pharmacist, so that the dispensing pharmacist's position follows from it: a transmission missing one of the listed particulars is not one the paragraph authorised the prescriber to make, and it should not be filled as transmitted until the missing particular has been supplied.

Be identified by name in the particulars the prescribing pharmacist supplies to the dispensing pharmacist, so the physician's identity travels with each prescription the pharmacist issues under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7).

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility
role_duties.duty: Use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and make sure that written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist as a Board of Registration in Pharmacy licensee
role_duties.duty: Meet all applicable Board requirements established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00, because 105 CMR 700.003(G)(1) makes that a requirement of the Department's prescribing power.
Issue, modify or discontinue in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and the collaborative practice agreement, as 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3) requires.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist who has issued, modified or discontinued a prescription
role_duties.duty: Provide a copy of the initial prescription, or of the modification or discontinuation, to the supervising physician within 24 hours of its issuance, and sooner where the circumstances require more urgent notification.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist practising in a retail setting
role_duties.duty: Confine prescriptions for controlled substances to Schedule VI, which is what 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) permits in that setting.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist holding controlled substances for immediate treatment
role_duties.duty: Dispense for immediate treatment only what 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorises her to prescribe, order from a wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor only Schedule VI substances she is authorized to prescribe, obtain Schedule II through V stock for that purpose only as supplied by the supervising physician or through a prescription or medication order for the patient, and maintain a record of any controlled substance so maintained.

common_traps.text: Ranking issuing, modifying and discontinuing by clinical gravity and assuming the greater authority includes the lesser. The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) state the three acts in parallel and authorise each one only as authorized in the agreement.
Treating a decision to stop a therapy as a clinical judgement outside the regulation. Discontinuation is one of the three regulated prescribing acts.

Reading the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as descriptive detail. The opening sentence ends provided the following requirements are met, which makes them requirements; the only refinement is that some are duties and some are permissions carrying conditions of their own.
Accepting an existing controlled substance registration whatever it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing.
Applying the DEA limb uniformly, either requiring it of every collaborating pharmacist or dismissing it as boilerplate. It is qualified by the words if applicable and points to 21 CFR 1300.

Merging the two registration requirements. The Department registration in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is a condition on the prescribing power; the controlled substance registration in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. is a qualification that must be maintained for the term of the agreement.

Attaching the section 18(e) training to the agreement. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2. makes it a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, and it is required before the registration is first obtained as well as at least biennially thereafter.

Supplying the particulars an ordinary prescriber would give and omitting the supervising physician's name, or offering a callback number in place of the work address. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) lists both, separately.

Writing an outpatient prescription for a facility inpatient, or entering the medication order on a record the pharmacy keeps. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) fixes both the instrument and the record it must be entered on.
Transplanting the facility medication order into a setting that holds no health facility licence because its records look similar. The paragraph is framed for a patient in a licensed health facility.

Revising the deadlines of collaborative prescribing without 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10). It is the one requirement in the paragraph fixed to a clock: 24 hours from issuance, to the supervising physician, and for a modification or a discontinuation as much as for an initial prescription.

Measuring the 24 hours in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) from the wrong event, or reading its proviso as an extension. The period runs from issuance, and more urgent notification under the circumstances shortens it.
Taking the best-known paragraphs for the whole of 105 CMR 700.003(G). There are ten numbered requirements, and (1), (3), (4), (5), (6), (9) and (10) each do work of their own.

Treating 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) as imposing a duty on the dispensing pharmacist. The paragraph conditions the prescribing pharmacist's power to issue, and the consequence for the receiving pharmacist is that an incomplete transmission is not one the paragraph authorised.

Reading authority to prescribe a Schedule II through V substance as authority to buy it in for immediate treatment. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(6) confines that stock to what the supervising physician supplies or what comes through a prescription or medication order for the patient.
